prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1293; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep it brief. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Houston, on one of the main freeways, heading toward the downtown exit. Traffic was moving but not fast.
Q: What lane were you in, and what were you doing at the time?
A: I was in the middle lane. I wanted to move into the right lane because my exit was coming up, so I checked my mirror and eased over.
Q: Did you signal before moving over?
A: I believe I did. I had the turn signal on for a few seconds before I started to move.
Q: What happened next?
A: As I was moving over, the car on my right sort of drifted into me. I felt a bump on the passenger side and my car pulled a little toward the shoulder. The other driver kept going for a second before they stopped.
Q: Were you able to see the other vehicle's lane position before you moved?
A: Not completely. It was in my blind spot for a moment, and I didn't see it until I was already partway over.
Q: Did you or the other driver exchange information at the scene?
A: Yes, we swapped insurance and contact details. The other driver seemed shaken but was polite.
Q: Have you been seen by a medical provider since the collision?
A: Yes. I've been having pain in my neck and lower back. It's mostly stiffness and soreness, and it gets worse when I sit for long periods. I've been seeing a doctor and doing some physical therapy.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal and I'd appreciate a timely response on the claim.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
